newsitem.title: CHINA: China forex reserves $95.363 bln end-September.
newsitem.headline: China forex reserves $95.363 bln end-September.

text.p: China's foreign exchange reserves reached $95.363 billion at the end of September, the central bank, the People's Bank of China, said in a third-quarter report published in the Financial News on Thursday.
Chinese officials have said China's foreign exchange reserves could exceed $100 billion by the end of this year.
The reserves have been growing steadily to more than $93 billion at the end of August from $90.7 billion at the start of the month.
China's foreign reserves were $73.5 billion at the end of 1995.
Central bank Governor Dai Xianglong told Reuters this week that reserves were at a comfortable level but hardly excessive.
"For a country of China's size, (the level of foreign exchange reserves) is not a big sum. We can only say it is comfortable," he said.
Most of the reserves -- about 70 percent -- were held in dollars, he said.
